historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun, The Muqaddimah, 1377-1382 CE, Andalusia (Spain): In his seminal work, Ibn Khaldun discusses the rise and fall of Islamic dynasties, including the Almohads. He mentions a region called Al-Khassal, which translates to 'the sandy' or 'desolate' region, likely referring to the arid lands of southeastern Spain. The Almohads, who ruled much of the Muslim world at the time, are known to have had military bases and settlements in this area.

Al-Idrisi, The Description of the World, 1154 CE, Morocco: Al-Idrisi, an Andalusian geographer, describes a region known as Al-Khassal, which is located northeast of Sus in Morocco. He mentions it as a fertile area with abundant water resources, and notes that it was once the seat of powerful Berber kingdoms. Al-Khassal's strategic location between the coastal regions and the desert made it a significant center of trade and political power in the medieval Islamic world.
